cases.sentence: Хотя госпожа Хохлакова проживала большею частию в ___, где имела поместье, или в Москве, где имела собственный дом, но и в нашем городке у нее был свой дом, доставшийся от отцов и дедов.
cases.explain: «другой губернии» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: At the Hohlakovs’ Alyosha soon reached Madame Hohlakov’s house, a handsome stone house of two stories, one of the finest in our town. Though Madame Hohlakov spent most of her time in another province where she had an estate, or in Moscow, where she had a house of her own, yet she had a house in our town too, inherited from her forefathers. The estate in our district was the largest of her three estates, yet she had been very little in our province before this time. She ran out to Alyosha in the hall.

cases.explain: «новом чуде» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Did you get my letter about the new miracle?” She spoke rapidly and nervously.

cases.sentence: — Maman, это с вами теперь истерика, а не со мной, — прощебетал вдруг в щелочку голосок Lise из ___.
cases.explain: «боковой комнаты» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Maman, it’s you who are hysterical now, not I,” Lise’s voice caroled through a tiny crack of the door at the side. Her voice sounded as though she wanted to laugh, but was doing her utmost to control it. Alyosha at once noticed the crack, and no doubt Lise was peeping through it, but that he could not see.

cases.sentence: — Мама, ради Бога, принесите корпию; корпию и этой едкой ___ для порезов, ну как ее зовут!
cases.explain: «мутной воды» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Some lint, mamma, for mercy’s sake, bring some lint and that muddy caustic lotion for wounds, what’s it called? We’ve got some. You know where the bottle is, mamma; it’s in your bedroom in the right-hand cupboard, there’s a big bottle of it there with the lint.”

cases.sentence: Мама, вы сами знаете, где стклянка, в спальне вашей в шкапике направо, там ___ и корпия…
cases.explain: «большая стклянка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Some lint, mamma, for mercy’s sake, bring some lint and that muddy caustic lotion for wounds, what’s it called? We’ve got some. You know where the bottle is, mamma; it’s in your bedroom in the right-hand cupboard, there’s a big bottle of it there with the lint.”

cases.sentence: Алеша, инстинктом чувствуя, что для нее время до возвращения мамаши дорого, — поспешно, много выпустив и сократив, но, однако, точно и ясно, передал ей о ___ своей со школьниками.
cases.explain: «загадочной встрече» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Instinctively feeling that the time of her mother’s absence was precious for her, Alyosha hastened to tell her of his enigmatic meeting with the schoolboys in the fewest words possible. Lise clasped her hands at his story.

cases.sentence: — гневно вскричала она, как будто даже имея какое-то право над ним, — да вы сами после того мальчик, самый ___, какой только может быть!
cases.explain: «маленький мальчик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “How can you, and in that dress too, associate with schoolboys?” she cried angrily, as though she had a right to control him. “You are nothing but a boy yourself if you can do that, a perfect boy! But you must find out for me about that horrid boy and tell me all about it, for there’s some mystery in it. Now for the second thing, but first a question: does the pain prevent you talking about utterly unimportant things, but talking sensibly?”

cases.sentence: Однако вы непременно разузнайте мне как-нибудь про этого ___ и мне все расскажите, потому что тут какой-то секрет.
cases.explain: «скверного мальчишку» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “How can you, and in that dress too, associate with schoolboys?” she cried angrily, as though she had a right to control him. “You are nothing but a boy yourself if you can do that, a perfect boy! But you must find out for me about that horrid boy and tell me all about it, for there’s some mystery in it. Now for the second thing, but first a question: does the pain prevent you talking about utterly unimportant things, but talking sensibly?”

cases.sentence: Затем я буду продолжать курс и сдам экзамен, а как придет ___, мы и женимся.
cases.explain: «законный срок» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Not at all. As soon as I read it, I thought that all that would come to pass, for as soon as Father Zossima dies, I am to leave the monastery. Then I shall go back and finish my studies, and when you reach the legal age we will be married. I shall love you. Though I haven’t had time to think about it, I believe I couldn’t find a better wife than you, and Father Zossima tells me I must marry.”

cases.sentence: Ангел мама, вы начинаете говорить чрезвычайно ___.
cases.explain: «остроумные вещи» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “But I couldn’t tell that he would come with a bad finger, or else perhaps I might have done it on purpose. My darling mamma, you begin to say really witty things.”
